title: Oppression of Cushan-rishathaim (8 years)
summary: Israel serves Cushan-rishathaim king of Mesopotamia eight years (Judg 3:8), the first oppression of the judges period.
description: Judges-period record added from James B. Jordan's chronology (secondary display) with Ussher, Jones and, where available, CFAH-1 Table 1 dates for sorting. Jordan treats the judgeships as partly overlapping regional sequences (North / Centre / South) fitted to the 480 years of 1 Kgs 6:1 and the 300 years of Judg 11:26.

sorting_basis.note: Tier 3: Ussher-Jones (F. N. Jones): 1418 BC (no higher-tier year available). Jordan (secondary display) never sets the sort.

chronologies.date: "1418 BC / 2586 AM": 8 years of Cushan-rishathaim, 1418–1410 BC ("THIS BRINGS US TO 1152 + 266 = 1418 BC FOR OTHNIEL")
chronologies.citation: Jones, Chart No. 4 "Judges to the First 3 Kings" (© 1993 Floyd Jones; chart text revised "As of 2007"), timeline band
chronologies.note: The 15th ed. (2002), ch. V p. 91, fixed "Cushan's dominion over Israel at BC 1400" with a 44-year Joshua-Judges chasm (1444 – 1400). That older figure is kept here and does not set the year. Chart 4 (revised as of 2007) gives 1418 BC. The 23rd ed. (2026), p. 88, prints "fix the date of Cushan's dominion over Israel at 1418 BC (Chart 4)" and "1444 – 1418 = 26 (the Joshua-Judges chasm)". Appendix F prints "2586 1418 Subjugation by Chushan-Rishathaim". The 23rd ed. agrees with the chart, so 1418 BC remains the year.

chronologies.date: 2591d AM, 1413 BC ("This was the first calamity of theirs and lasted eight years")
chronologies.citation: Ussher, Annals of the World, Fourth Age §341 (paragraph numbering of the modern transcription)

chronologies.date: "2620 - Beginning of 8-year oppression of Cushan (Jud. 3:8). Israel had been faithful for the 35 years after the death of Joshua, during the time of the elders who succeeded him."
chronologies.citation: Jordan, From Creation to Solomon (Studies in Biblical Chronology No. 2, Biblical Horizons, Oct. 2001), ch. 11 "The Era of the Judges and the Reign of Saul", p. 51
chronologies.note: 2001 revision. Jordan's 1991 list (BC 3:8) has an earlier year; see the second Jordan entry. p. 46: "we come to AM 2620, which would be 60 years after the division of the land in 2560."

chronologies.date: "2594 - End of the period of peace during and after Joshua, beginning of 8-year oppression of Cushan (Jud. 3:8)."
chronologies.citation: Jordan, "Chronology and Kings (II)," Biblical Chronology 3:8 (August 1991), section "The Judges", summary list
chronologies.note: 1991 scheme, superseded by Jordan himself in 2001 (Studies in Biblical Chronology No. 2 dates the whole judges sequence 26 years later because he there ends the 300 years of Judg 11:26 when Ammon took the villages, AM 2860, not at Jephthah's victory). BC 5:2 (Feb. 1993): "In the year 2594 began the eight-year oppression of Cushan-Rishathaim of Mesopotamia".

chronologies.date: 2620 AM 8 year oppression of Cushan begins. (Jud.3:8)
chronologies.citation: Anno Mundi Chronology Studies (unnamed compiler; a compilation of James B. Jordan's system), p. 6, chart "Year of the World: From Joseph’s death to the Judges"
chronologies.note: Agrees with Jordan's own published AM 2620.
